prov.l: Provision for Loan, Lease, and Other Losses

prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
For the nine month period ended September 30, 2026, we recorded a provision for credit losses of $1,000,000, which represents a decrease of $875,000 from the $1,875,000 provision recorded in the corresponding nine months of last year. The decrease in the provision is due to the updated loss driver analysis completed in the first quarter of 2026 offset by increases in qualitative factors related international and national economic conditions related to the Iran conflict and the impact it may have on agricultural loans due to higher diesel and fertilizer prices and an increase in the qualitative factor for changes in the volume and severity of past due loans for commercial relationships due to the increase in non-accrual loans. (see “Financial Condition – Allowance for Credit Losses and Credit Quality Risk”).

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, no provision was recorded, which represents a decrease of $500,000 from the $500,000 provision recorded in the corresponding three months of last year. The decrease in the provision for off-balance sheet items was due to a decrease in the reserve associated with the commitment for student loan lending. The on-balance sheet provision for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was impacted by the increase in non-accrual loans and the qualitative factors noted for the nine month period.

nonint.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonint.text:
The following tables reflect the breakdown of non-interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 (dollars in thousands):

Non-interest expenses increased $1,933,000, or 4.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Salaries and employee benefits increased $992,000 or 3.3%. Full time equivalent employees (FTE) increased 10.1 or 2.7% when comparing 2026 to 2025. This increase in headcount in addition to merit increases resulted in payroll and payroll taxes increasing by $939,000. Due to actuarial assumptions, post retirement benefits decreased $47,000. As a result of the decrease in brokerage and insurance commissions due to the resignation of a broker in the third quarter of 2025, commission expense decreased $182,000. Health insurance associated expenses have increased $247,000 due to higher claims and stop loss insurance rates.

The increase in OREO expenses for the three and nine month periods is due to legal fees and real estate taxes associated with non-accrual loans and foreclosed properties. The decrease in FDIC expense for the nine month periods presented is due to an increase in the Bank’s leverage ratio in 2026 compared to 2025. The decrease in other expenses for the three month period ended September 30, 2026 is due to a recovery of amounts previously charged-off in the first quarter of 2026.

nonop.heading: Non-interest Expense
nonop.text:
The following tables reflect the breakdown of non-interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 (dollars in thousands):

Non-interest expenses increased $1,933,000, or 4.0% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025. Salaries and employee benefits increased $992,000 or 3.3%. Full time equivalent employees (FTE) increased 10.1 or 2.7% when comparing 2026 to 2025. This increase in headcount in addition to merit increases resulted in payroll and payroll taxes increasing by $939,000. Due to actuarial assumptions, post retirement benefits decreased $47,000. As a result of the decrease in brokerage and insurance commissions due to the resignation of a broker in the third quarter of 2025, commission expense decreased $182,000. Health insurance associated expenses have increased $247,000 due to higher claims and stop loss insurance rates.

The increase in OREO expenses for the three and nine month periods is due to legal fees and real estate taxes associated with non-accrual loans and foreclosed properties. The decrease in FDIC expense for the nine month periods presented is due to an increase in the Bank’s leverage ratio in 2026 compared to 2025. The decrease in other expenses for the three month period ended September 30, 2026 is due to a recovery of amounts previously charged-off in the first quarter of 2026.

tax.heading: Provision for Income Taxes
tax.text: The provision for income taxes was $7,100,000 for the nine month period ended September 30, 2026 compared to $6,213,000 for the same period in 2025. The increase is primarily attributable to the increase in income before the provision for income taxes of $7,282,000 for the comparable periods due increase in net interest income after the provision for credit losses. Through management of our municipal loan and bond portfolios, management is focused on minimizing our effective tax rate. Our effective tax rate was 17.9% and 19.2% for the first nine months of 2026 and 2025, respectively, compared to the federal statutory rate of 21%.

net.text: The Company had net income of $32,484,000 for the first nine months of 2026 compared to $26,089,000 for last year’s comparable period, an increase of $6,395,000, or 24.5%, primarily due to an increase in net interest income after the provision for credit losses of $8,149,000. Basic earnings per share for the first nine months of 2026 was $6.77, compared to $5.44 for last year’s comparable period, representing a 24.5% increase. Annualized return on assets and return on equity for the nine months of 2026 were 1.37% and 12.36%, respectively, compared with 1.16% and 11.15% for last year’s comparable period.

ocf.text: Cash generated by operating activities, investing activities and financing activities influences liquidity management. Our Company’s historical activity in this area can be seen in the Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows. The most important source of funds is core deposits. Repayment of principal on outstanding loans and cash flows created from the investment portfolio are also factors in liquidity management. Other sources of funding include brokered certificates of deposit and the sale of loans or investments, if needed.

da.text: Premises and equipment decreased $429,000 to $20,569,000 as of September 30, 2026 from December 31, 2025 as a result of depreciation.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
Net interest income, the most significant component of the Company’s earnings, is the amount by which interest income generated from interest-earning assets exceeds interest expense paid on interest-bearing liabilities.

Net interest income for the first nine months of 2026 was $79,064,000, an increase of $7,274,000, or 10.1%, compared to the same period in 2025. For the first nine months of 2026 the provision for credit losses was $1,000,000. The provision for the first nine months of 2025 was $1,875,000. Consequently, net interest income after the provision for credit losses was $78,064,000 in the first nine months of 2026 compared to $69,915,000 during the first nine months of 2025.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, net interest income was $27,257,000 compared to $25,140,000, an increase of $2,117,000, or 8.4%, over the comparable period in 2025. There was no provision for credit losses in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $500,000 in 2025. Consequently, net interest income after the provision for credit losses was $27,257,000 for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to $24,640,000 in 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Debt securities
lines.why: Bonds held for sale or to maturity: financial.

lines.name: Loans, net of the allowance
lines.why: Lending is a bank's business: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Deposits
lines.why: Customers' money a bank holds is its business: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.

accounts.name: Equity
accounts.note: Other comprehensive income (currency translation, unrealised gains) moves equity without passing through net income: it is in the residual.

s.t: The law requires that certain supervisory actions be taken against undercapitalized institutions, the severity of which depends on the degree of undercapitalization.
An institution’s assessment rate depends upon the category to which it is assigned, and certain adjustments specified by FDIC regulations.
The Bank’s primary source of funding is customer deposits, gathered throughout its network of banking offices.
Because of the Bank’s concentration of business activities in its market area, the Company’s financial condition and results of operations depend upon economic conditions in its market areas.
Our ability to pay dividends to our shareholders largely depends on our receipt of dividends from the Bank .
We rely on our management and other key personnel, and the loss of any of them may adversely affect our operations.
In addition, we will continue to depend on our ability to retain and recruit key commercial and agricultural loan officers.
Our operations rely on the secure processing, storage, and transmission of confidential and other information in our computer systems and networks.

The Company’s Board of Directors expects that comparable cash dividends will continue to be paid by the Company in the future; however, future dividends necessarily depend upon earnings, financial condition, appropriate legal restrictions and other factors in existence at the time the Board of Directors considers a dividend distribution.
The Company’s primary source of income is dividends received from the Bank.

Under ASC Topic 606, management determined that the primary sources of revenue emanating from interest and dividend income on loans and investments along with noninterest revenue resulting from investment security gains, loan servicing, gains on loans sold and earnings on bank owned life insurances are not within the scope of this topic.
